baseline_exact: Do not assume help has been dispatched if you cannot confirm that a message was received. @ED
a02_exact: Do not assume responders were notified without confirmation. Use the next safe communication option in your trip plan. @T06,ED

baseline_exact: Life-threatening arm or leg bleeding uncontrolled by firm direct pressure when a commercial windlass tourniquet and training are available.
a02_exact: Life-threatening bleeding from a visible arm or leg wound when a suitable commercial tourniquet is available.

baseline_exact: Commercial high/tight above joint | Lock windlass & log exact time | Leave visible for EMS; never loosen
a02_exact: Visible limb wound | Place clear of joint toward torso | Tighten and leave for EMS

baseline_exact: Correct versus incorrect configuration contrasting proper commercial tourniquet placement and time logging against hazardous thin improvised straps or joint placement. Conceptual, not to scale.
a02_exact: Placement decision for a visible extremity wound. Follow exact device directions and instructor guidance.

baseline_exact: Place a commercial tourniquet high and tight on the injured arm or leg—at least 2 to 3 inches above the wound and NEVER directly over a knee or elbow joint—and tighten the windlass until bright bleeding stops completely. @M02
a02_exact: For life-threatening arm or leg bleeding with a visible wound, follow training and the device directions. Place a commercial tourniquet 2 to 3 inches toward the torso from the wound, clear of any joint, and tighten until bleeding stops. @M02

baseline_exact: Never loosen or remove a tourniquet placed for life-threatening bleeding in the field; hospital surgical teams manage definitive removal. @M02
a02_exact: Leave the tourniquet in place for medical personnel. Do not loosen it during evacuation. @M02

baseline_exact: If bleeding persists after tightening one properly placed commercial tourniquet, apply a second commercial tourniquet directly above the first if available and expedite EMS rescue. @M02,T02
a02_exact: If bleeding continues after correct placement and maximum tightening, follow your training or dispatcher instructions. The Red Cross describes a second commercial tourniquet above the first when available. @M02

baseline_exact: Unresponsive + no normal breath | Call 911 & fetch AED immediately | Follow trained or dispatcher CPR
a02_exact: Unresponsive with absent or abnormal breathing | Call 911, start CPR and get AED | Follow age, cause and AED prompts

baseline_exact: Call 911 immediately on speakerphone, send a bystander for an AED if near a trailhead or building, and begin firm center-of-chest compressions per certified CPR training or live 911 dispatcher coaching. @M03,T02
a02_exact: Call 911 on speaker, send someone for an AED if available, and start CPR as directed. Tell dispatch if the patient is an infant or child or if the arrest followed submersion. Breaths are important in pediatric and drowning arrests. @M03,M25,M26

baseline_exact: Confirm 911 is active, compressions follow dispatcher or certified-course rhythm, and responders rotate every two minutes when teammates are present to prevent fatigue. @M03,ED
a02_exact: Confirm emergency activation and follow dispatcher, training and AED prompts. Avoid unnecessary interruptions in compressions. @M03,M25

baseline_exact: Stop compressions only if the scene becomes unsafe, clear normal breathing/movement resumes, an AED instructs hands-off analysis, or EMS assumes care. @M03,T01
a02_exact: An AED pause for analysis or shock is temporary. Resume CPR when prompted unless normal breathing returns, the scene becomes unsafe, or EMS takes over. @M03,M25

baseline_exact: Forceful cough -> encourage only | Silent obstruction -> 911 + aid | Unresponsive -> CPR; zero blind sweeps
a02_exact: Effective cough: watch | Severe blockage: 911 and age-specific care | Unresponsive: guided CPR

baseline_exact: If the person can cough forcefully or speak, stay beside them and encourage continued coughing without slapping their back or interfering with their own airway clearing. @M04
a02_exact: If the person is coughing effectively, encourage coughing and watch for a weak cough, inability to speak or breathe, or worsening responsiveness. @M04

baseline_exact: If the person is silent, clutches their throat, cannot cough or speak, or turns bluish, call 911 immediately and apply trained back blows/abdominal thrusts (or live dispatcher-guided steps). @M04,T02
a02_exact: Call 911 for severe obstruction. Follow dispatcher or age-appropriate training. Adults and children use a different thrust technique from infants. Tell dispatch if the patient is an infant, in late pregnancy, or cannot be encircled. @M04,M25

baseline_exact: If a choking person becomes unresponsive, lower them safely to firm ground, confirm 911 is activated, and begin dispatcher-guided or trained CPR—never perform blind finger sweeps into the throat. @M04,M03
a02_exact: If the person becomes unresponsive, begin dispatcher-guided CPR. Remove an object only if you see it when opening the airway. Never sweep blindly. @M04,M25

baseline_exact: Confirm normal speech and easy breathing return after any obstruction clears, and arrange medical evaluation after abdominal thrusts or persistent coughing. @M04,ED
a02_exact: Monitor breathing and responsiveness until advanced care arrives. @M04,M25

baseline_exact: Verify normal rhythmic breathing and absence of high-force fall or neck/back trauma before rolling the patient; if spinal injury is suspected, leave them in place unless vomiting or fluid threatens the airway. @M22,M11
a02_exact: Call 911 and check for normal breathing. For suspected neck, back, hip or pelvic injury, avoid unnecessary movement and follow the dispatcher if the airway is threatened. @M22,M03

baseline_exact: Insulate the patient from cold ground, stay beside them continuously, and recheck normal breathing every few minutes until EMS arrives. @M22,E05,M20
a02_exact: Stay with the person and continuously watch their breathing. Gasping is abnormal. If breathing stops or becomes abnormal, roll them onto their back and start dispatcher-guided CPR. @M22,M03

baseline_exact: Leaving an unresponsive breathing person flat on their back where the tongue or vomit can silently obstruct the airway. @M22
a02_exact: Leaving the person unmonitored in a side position can delay recognition of respiratory arrest. @M22

baseline_exact: Call 911 immediately and expose the junctional wound completely so pressure lands straight on the bleeding vessel rather than surrounding tissue. @M01,T02
a02_exact: Call 911, ensure scene safety and find the source of life-threatening bleeding when this can be done safely. @M01,T02

baseline_exact: Apply firm, continuous, uninterrupted direct pressure straight into the bleeding source; responders trained in Stop the Bleed may pack clean or hemostatic gauze tightly into deep groin/armpit cavities (NEVER pack the neck, chest, or abdomen) and hold continuous pressure. @M01
a02_exact: Apply firm, continuous direct pressure. Follow current bleeding-control training or dispatcher instructions for wound packing and only when the wound location is appropriate. Do not improvise packing a body cavity. @M01,M02

baseline_exact: Keep the patient warm and insulated against shock while maintaining steady downward pressure without releasing to check until EMS assumes control. @M01,M05
a02_exact: Keep effective pressure in place while waiting for emergency care and keep the person warm. @M01,M05

baseline_exact: For electrical injury, NEVER touch the person until the power source is confirmed shut off by utility/breaker controls (stay well back from downed power lines and call 911); remember electrical burns cause severe hidden internal tissue and heart-rhythm damage even with tiny skin marks. @M07,T01,D04
a02_exact: Stay back from energized equipment, floodwater or downed lines. Call 911 and approach only after qualified personnel or the dispatcher confirm the area is safe. @M07,T02

baseline_exact: For dry chemical powders on skin, brush loose dry powder off with gloved hands or cloth BEFORE flushing continuously with copious cool running water for at least 20 minutes while removing contaminated clothing. @M07,M15
a02_exact: For chemical skin exposure, keep yourself clear of contamination, start decontamination as directed by the product label and Poison Control, and remove contaminated clothing if safe. For many liquid splashes, start rinsing promptly with running water. Identify dry or water-reactive material to dispatch rather than improvising its treatment. @M15,M16

baseline_exact: Call 911 for ALL electrical burns, chemical eye splashes, large/painful chemical burns, or breathing irritation, and save the exact chemical label for Poison Control/EMS. @M07,M16,T02
a02_exact: Call 911 for serious electrical injury, breathing difficulty or collapse. Contact Poison Control promptly for substance-specific skin or eye instructions. Read the label from a safe location. @M15,M16,M18,T02

baseline_exact: Rolled jackets/packs for gentle side-of-head cushioning, ground insulation where reachable without shifting, and emergency comms.
a02_exact: A reliable emergency communication device and insulation that can be placed without moving the patient.

baseline_exact: High fall / neck pain / tingling | Hold head & neck still as found | Wait for trained EMS packaging
a02_exact: Guard scene and call 911 | Avoid unnecessary movement | Airway or immediate danger may change the plan

baseline_exact: Correct versus incorrect spinal care contrasting neutral in-place stabilization and EMS activation against pulling the patient upright or twisting the neck. Conceptual, not to scale.
a02_exact: Decision diagram showing when airway care or an immediate scene hazard calls for reassessing movement with dispatch.

baseline_exact: Instruct an alert patient immediately to stay completely still and look straight ahead—do NOT twist, nod, sit up, or let bystanders pull them to their feet after a high-mechanism impact. @M11,T01
a02_exact: Ask the person to remain still and avoid unnecessary movement. Activate 911 and describe the impact, symptoms and any continuing scene threat. @M22,M11,T02

baseline_exact: Gently stabilize the head in the neutral position found using hands or snug rolled clothing beside the ears (never force a crooked neck straight or apply traction) while activating 911/SAR. @M11,T02
a02_exact: Let the patient remain in the position found unless airway care or immediate scene danger requires movement. Do not force the head into alignment or improvise a rigid collar. @M22

baseline_exact: Check whether the patient can feel and wiggle fingers and toes without moving their spine, keep them protected from wind/cold, and leave definitive spinal packaging to trained EMS crews. @M11,M09,E05
a02_exact: Monitor breathing and alertness, avoid heat loss and follow the dispatcher on any movement or assessment. @M22,M11,T03

baseline_exact: Activate 911/SAR immediately—open fractures carry high risk of severe bleeding, deep bone infection, and permanent limb loss requiring urgent hospital surgery and IV antibiotics. @M09,T02
a02_exact: Call 911 for a suspected open fracture. Report the injury, severe bleeding and any change in alertness or limb color. @M09,M01,T02

baseline_exact: Control active external bleeding with gentle clean gauze pressure around the wound edges without pressing directly on exposed bone fragments, and NEVER push protruding bone back beneath the skin. @M09,M01
a02_exact: Use emergency bleeding-control guidance for life-threatening blood loss. Keep pressure off protruding bone itself and do not push bone back into the wound. @M01,M02,M09

baseline_exact: Cover exposed bone and tissue gently with clean sterile dressing, pad and immobilize the limb in the position found, insulate the patient against shock, and keep strictly NPO. @M09,M05,M06
a02_exact: Protect the wound with a clean dressing. Follow dispatch on moving or supporting the limb, and monitor breathing, alertness and circulation while waiting for help. @M09,M22

baseline_exact: For chemical splashes, start flushing immediately with copious gentle streams of clean potable water or sterile saline for at least 15 to 20 continuous minutes, tilting the head so rinse water drains OUTWARD away from the unaffected eye. @M18,W29
a02_exact: For a chemical splash, begin rinsing immediately with plenty of room-temperature running water. Continue for 15–20 minutes at minimum as directed by Poison Control. Do not delay while looking for sterile saline. @M18

baseline_exact: Remove contact lenses gently if they do not flush out on their own (never force a stuck lens), instruct the person NOT to rub the eye, and keep eyelids gently held open during chemical irrigation. @M18
a02_exact: Remove contact lenses if you can do so easily without delaying rinsing. Encourage blinking. Do not rub the eye or try to remove an embedded object. @M18

baseline_exact: Seek urgent medical/ophthalmology evaluation for ALL chemical eye splashes, persistent grit feeling after gentle flushing, blurred vision, or severe light sensitivity. @M18,T02
a02_exact: Contact Poison Control during or after irrigation for substance-specific next steps. Severe pain, impaired vision or a major exposure needs emergency evaluation. @M15,M18

baseline_exact: Any chemical splash, vision loss, severe pain, or object stuck on the eyeball surface halts travel and requires immediate clinical eye care. @M18,T02
a02_exact: If an object is embedded or penetration is suspected, avoid pressure and seek emergency care. This is a different branch from chemical irrigation. @M18

baseline_exact: Confusion/no shiver -> severe emergency | Keep horizontal & handle ultra-gently | Wrap dry, warm trunk only & call 911
a02_exact: Call for urgent help | Handle gently and insulate | Follow dispatcher for abnormal breathing

baseline_exact: Apply gentle insulated external warmth ONLY to the trunk (armpits, chest, groin—never direct scalding heat or hot immersion of arms/legs), withhold oral fluids if confused or drowsy, and monitor breathing carefully for a full minute before deciding on CPR per dispatcher guidance. @M23,M03
a02_exact: Keep insulation in place and use protected trunk warming within your training. Withhold oral fluids if alertness is impaired. If the person does not respond or breathe normally, activate 911 and follow dispatcher advice without inserting a fixed lay waiting period. @M23,M03,T03

baseline_exact: Call 911 immediately after any cold-water immersion, move the survivor gently out of wind into shelter, and keep them lying horizontal rather than letting them walk vigorously right after exit. @X02,M23,T02
a02_exact: Call 911 after significant cold immersion, breathing trouble or altered alertness. Once the person is safely out of the water, shelter them from wind, handle them gently and follow the dispatcher on position and movement. @M23,M26,T03

baseline_exact: Any submersion -> assess breath & 911 | Never press belly to "drain water" | Monitor hours; clinical lung evaluation
a02_exact: Safe recovery from water | Call 911 for red flags | Drowning CPR includes breaths when able

baseline_exact: Activate 911 immediately for ANY submersion involving loss of consciousness, cessation of breathing, persistent coughing, foamy sputum, chest discomfort, or blue lips; if unresponsive and not breathing normally, start trained/dispatcher CPR immediately. @M03,X02,T02
a02_exact: Call 911 for unresponsiveness, abnormal breathing, persistent cough or breathing difficulty after submersion. Once on safe ground, follow the dispatcher. CPR for drowning includes rescue breaths and chest compressions when the rescuer can provide them. @M26,M03

baseline_exact: Even when a submerged person exits coughing and alert, remove wet layers, keep them resting warmly, and arrange prompt clinical medical evaluation—aspirated water can irritate lung linings and cause worsening breathing distress over subsequent hours. @X02,M23,M20
a02_exact: Keep a breathing patient warm and monitor closely. Ask dispatch about evaluation if coughing or breathing symptoms occurred, and report any deterioration immediately. @M26,T02

baseline_exact: Refreeze risk -> protect frozen & exit | Never use stoves/flames on numb skin | Zero refreeze -> controlled warm thaw + MD
a02_exact: Can tissue refreeze? | Protect and evacuate | Qualified advice before water rewarming

baseline_exact: If safe definitive shelter and rapid transport with ZERO refreezing risk exist, follow qualified clinical/WMS controlled warm-water rewarming protocols (clean circulating water ~98–102°F), cushion gently between digits with dry sterile gauze without popping blisters, and transport promptly. @M24,T04
a02_exact: When refreezing remains possible, protect the frozen area and prioritize evacuation. Ask qualified medical support before controlled water rewarming. Use the WMS protocol only when its water temperature, protection and no-refreezing conditions can be met. @M24,T04

baseline_exact: Confirm zero refreezing risk before any thaw, zero dry-flame heat exposure, and clean padded digit separation for evacuation. @M24,T04
a02_exact: Confirm the evacuation plan avoids refreezing and that the tissue is protected from friction, pressure and direct heat. @M24,T04

baseline_exact: Confusion/slurred speech/collapse + heat | Call 911 & cool aggressively NOW | Zero forced oral fluids; hospital mandatory
a02_exact: Call 911 and cool promptly | Protect airway during cooling | Continue to medical care

baseline_exact: Begin aggressive external cooling IMMEDIATELY while waiting for EMS: immerse the trunk/limbs in cold water if safely available (keeping head and airway strictly supported above water), OR douse continuously with cold water and cold wet towels rotated over neck, armpits, groin, and torso while fanning vigorously. @T05,T09
a02_exact: Start active cooling while EMS is on the way. Use cold-water immersion for an exertional case only when the airway can be continuously protected and adequate help is available. Otherwise cool the skin with water and airflow. Follow dispatch for the setting and patient. @T09,M27

baseline_exact: Do NOT force fluids by mouth into a confused, drowsy, or vomiting patient; follow 911 dispatcher directions continuously and obtain mandatory hospital clinical evaluation even if alertness briefly improves. @T09,M05
a02_exact: Give nothing by mouth to a confused, drowsy or vomiting patient. Continue dispatcher-guided cooling and emergency evaluation even if alertness improves. @T09,M27

baseline_exact: Assess lightning-strike casualties safely using reverse triage and CPR
a02_exact: Recognize ongoing lightning hazards and coordinate emergency care

baseline_exact: Victims hold zero residual charge | Reverse triage: non-breathing FIRST | Call 911, CPR/AED & full clinical exam
a02_exact: Check continuing strike risk | Tell 911 casualty count and breathing | Start safe dispatcher-guided care

baseline_exact: Four-step lightning-casualty plate showing scene check, safe immediate contact, reverse-triage CPR priority, and multi-system clinical evaluation. Conceptual, not to scale.
a02_exact: Rescue sequence separating the scene hazard from the electrical state of the patient.

baseline_exact: Check immediately whether active lightning still threatens the exact spot—if feasible, move casualties quickly to safer enclosed shelter or lower-risk ground, noting that lightning victims do NOT retain an electrical charge and are completely safe to touch immediately. @E07,T01,M03
a02_exact: Check ongoing lightning, terrain and electrical hazards before approaching. A lightning victim does not retain an electrical charge, but the site may still be dangerous. @M28,T01

baseline_exact: Apply lightning "reverse triage" when multiple people are hit: check unresponsive, non-breathing victims FIRST (because lightning frequently causes immediate survivable respiratory/cardiac arrest) while conscious crying/groaning victims are breathing. @M03,T02
a02_exact: With multiple casualties, tell 911 which people are unresponsive and not breathing normally. Begin resuscitation when safe and follow dispatch on priorities. @M28,M03

baseline_exact: Ongoing close lightning requires moving victims to safer ground rapidly while maintaining continuous CPR and EMS activation. @E07,M03
a02_exact: If ongoing lightning makes care unsafe, tell dispatch and follow its direction on movement and resuscitation. @M28,T01

baseline_exact: Hives + throat/breath/dizzy/vomit | Call 911 & assist OWN prescribed epi | Log time; never rely on antihistamines
a02_exact: Recognize a serious allergic reaction | Call 911 and help use prescribed device | Monitor for persistent or returning symptoms

baseline_exact: Recognize anaphylaxis immediately when exposure triggers ANY airway/breathing sign (swollen lips/tongue/throat, hoarseness, wheezing, trouble breathing), dizziness/fainting, widespread hives/flushing, or severe cramps/vomiting. @M08,T02
a02_exact: Suspect anaphylaxis when airway symptoms, breathing difficulty, faintness, or symptoms across more than one body system develop after a likely allergen. A severe reaction can occur without hives. @M08

baseline_exact: Call 911 immediately and assist the patient in administering their OWN prescribed epinephrine auto-injector into the outer mid-thigh strictly per the device label (can go through light clothing); log exact injection time. @M08,M20
a02_exact: Call 911 and assist promptly with the patient’s prescribed epinephrine auto-injector as directed by its instructions and their action plan. Record when it was used. @M08

baseline_exact: Do NOT delay epinephrine waiting for oral antihistamines to work, never use someone else's prescription without direct clinician/dispatcher authorization, and keep the patient lying flat (or seated upright if breathing is easier—never suddenly standing). @M08,M05
a02_exact: Do not wait for antihistamines. Avoid having the patient stand or walk. Follow dispatcher directions about positioning and monitor breathing. @M08

baseline_exact: If severe symptoms fail to improve or worsen after 5 to 15 minutes and the patient carries a second prescribed dose, follow the device/dispatcher directions and expedite EMS transport. @M08,T02
a02_exact: If symptoms persist or return, tell 911 immediately. Follow the action plan, product directions and dispatcher advice about a second device. @M08

baseline_exact: Move calmly out of striking range immediately—do NOT chase, kill, or try to capture the snake (which causes second bites); keep the bitten person calm, resting still, and call 911/EMS promptly for hospital antivenom evaluation. @M13,T01,T02
a02_exact: Move out of striking range, call 911 and keep the bitten person at rest. A photograph is optional only from a safe distance and without delaying care. Never try to catch or handle the snake. @M13,T02

baseline_exact: Save the exact chemical bottle, medication label, or intact plant/mushroom fragment (handled safely in a bag) plus approximate amount and time of exposure so toxicologists and clinicians can identify the exact agent. @M16,M20
a02_exact: Call U.S. Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222 for case-specific advice if the person is stable. Read the label or use a photo already taken safely. Do not gather or transport an unknown substance if that risks exposure. @M15,M16

baseline_exact: Stay calm, note the EXACT start time on a watch, clear hard rocks, fire pits, water edges, or sharp gear away from the person, and place a soft folded jacket beneath their head. @T01,M20
a02_exact: Time the seizure and move hazards away if safe. Protect the head with something soft. @M29,T01

baseline_exact: NEVER hold the person down, restrain jerking limbs, or put fingers, spoons, wallets, or sticks into their mouth (people cannot swallow their tongues, and forcing objects breaks teeth and blocks airways). @M04,M20
a02_exact: Do not hold the person down or place anything in their mouth. @M29

baseline_exact: Once shaking stops, check normal breathing and gently roll the person onto their side in the recovery position to keep the airway clear while monitoring them until fully awake; call 911 immediately if a seizure lasts over 5 minutes, repeats, occurs in water, involves injury/pregnancy/diabetes, or is a first-ever seizure. @M22,T02
a02_exact: Check breathing and use a safe side position when appropriate. Call 911 if it lasts longer than five minutes, repeats without recovery, happens in water, or causes injury, breathing or waking difficulty. Follow CDC or dispatcher directions for pregnancy, diabetes or a first seizure. @M29,M22

baseline_exact: Seizure exceeding 5 minutes, back-to-back seizures, breathing failure after shaking stops, or head/water injury demands immediate 911 response. @T02,M03
a02_exact: If the person is unresponsive and not breathing normally, activate 911 and start dispatcher-guided CPR. @M29,M03

baseline_exact: Awake & swallows -> own glucose + 15 m | Confused/drowsy -> ZERO oral intake | Unresponsive/no relief -> 911 & airway
a02_exact: Awake and swallowing: own action plan | Impaired alertness: nothing by mouth | Call 911 for severe signs

baseline_exact: ONLY if the person is fully awake, able to sit up, and swallowing safely without coughing, help them take their own fast-acting sugar (such as labeled glucose tablets, fruit juice, or regular sugary drink) and recheck symptoms after 15 minutes; follow with a balanced snack once alert. @M20,ED
a02_exact: If the person is fully awake and can swallow safely, assist with their own rapid glucose plan. Follow the plan and check whether symptoms resolve. @M30

baseline_exact: If the person is severely confused, drowsy, seizing, unable to swallow safely, or unresponsive, NEVER put food, liquid, or gel into their mouth (aspiration hazard)—call 911 immediately and place in recovery position if breathing normally (trained companions with the patient's own prescribed glucagon follow its exact label). @M22,T02,M05
a02_exact: For impaired alertness, seizure or inability to swallow, give nothing by mouth. Call 911 promptly and follow the patient’s emergency plan and dispatcher. @M30,M22

baseline_exact: Confirm swallowing safety before ANY oral sugar, recheck clarity at 15 minutes, and keep zero oral intake if drowsy or altered. @M20,M22
a02_exact: Confirm the patient is alert and swallowing safely before giving anything by mouth. Monitor for deterioration. @M30

baseline_exact: Failure to improve within 15 minutes, declining alertness, inability to swallow, or unresponsiveness requires immediate 911 emergency care. @T02,M22
a02_exact: Declining alertness, inability to swallow or unresponsiveness requires emergency help immediately. @M30,T02

baseline_exact: Recognize mask limits: bandanas, wet rags, and loose surgical masks do NOT filter fine wildfire smoke particles—only a properly fitted NIOSH-approved N95/P100 particulate respirator filters PM2.5, and NO particulate mask protects against carbon monoxide or low oxygen near active flames. @D06,C19
a02_exact: A well-fitting particulate respirator can reduce smoke particles. It cannot protect against carbon monoxide, toxic gases or oxygen deficiency. Follow local health alerts and evacuate when directed. @D06,D08

baseline_exact: Assess cold fast snowmelt stream crossings without risking foot entrapment
a02_exact: Recognize when a snowmelt stream requires a detour

baseline_exact: Evaluate swift mountain streams safely and recognize when high water requires turning back or waiting for morning lows.
a02_exact: Decide from the bank when to turn back or use an official crossing.

baseline_exact: Sturdy footwear worn across (never barefoot), trekking poles for third-point balance and unbuckled pack hip belt/sternum strap.
a02_exact: Current route information, alternate route, and time and insulation to wait safely outside the flood zone.

baseline_exact: Cross early before afternoon melt | Reject deep swift water & strainers | Shoes on; unbuckle pack straps
a02_exact: Assess from stable ground | Reject floodwater and unknown footing | Use maintained crossing or turn back

baseline_exact: Decision tree gating mountain stream crossings on morning snowmelt lows, depth/current limits, downstream strainer hazards and unbuckled pack safety. Conceptual, not to scale.
a02_exact: Decision schematic for rejecting uncertain crossings. It establishes no cutoff for safe wading.

baseline_exact: Time glacial and snowmelt stream crossings for EARLY MORNING—afternoon sun melts high snowpack rapidly, turning a calm ankle-deep morning creek into a roaring waist-deep torrent by 4 p.m. @X10,W25,E04
a02_exact: Assess from a stable bank. Heat, rain and upstream releases can alter snowmelt flow. Do not infer a safe hour or wading depth. @X10,W25,T16

baseline_exact: Scout carefully from the bank BEFORE stepping in: reject any crossing with fast waist-deep flow, rolling rocks audible underneath, murky silty water hiding holes, slippery logs, waterfalls/strainers (downed trees) immediately downstream or water above knee depth in swift current. @N10,T07,X10
a02_exact: Reject floodwater, hidden footing, strong current, ice-cold water, drop-offs or downstream obstructions. Find a maintained open bridge or another official route. @N10,T07,T16

baseline_exact: On a verified shallow, manageable crossing ONLY: keep sturdy shoes ON (protecting feet from slick rock cuts), UNBUCKLE pack hip-belt and sternum straps (so a heavy pack cannot pin you underwater if you slip) and face slightly upstream using poles or linked group support. @N10,E11,ED
a02_exact: If there is no verified safe route, turn back or wait outside the flood zone. Seek local guidance instead of improvised group wading. @N10,T16

baseline_exact: Confirm clear shallow footing, zero downstream log strainers/drops, shoes on and pack straps unbuckled before stepping off the bank. @N10,ED
a02_exact: Confirm the alternate route avoids the water and its downstream hazards. @N10,T16,ED

baseline_exact: Fast murky floodwater, water above knee depth in swift current, downstream log strainers or cold-water shock risk stops crossing—camp safely on the near bank until morning lows or turn back. @N10,T07,X02
a02_exact: Any flooding or uncertainty about footing, current or a safe exit stops the crossing. @N10,T07,T16

baseline_exact: Eliminate sudden cold-shock drowning by wearing a properly buckled life jacket whenever underway in small craft.
a02_exact: Reduce drowning risk by wearing a correctly fitted life jacket throughout small-craft travel.

baseline_exact: WEAR your buckled, properly fitted USCG-approved PFD continuously from dock launch to landing—sudden capsizes in cold water trigger 1-minute cold shock before anyone can dig stowed jackets out from under seats or buckle straps with numb fingers. @X04,X02
a02_exact: Wear a correctly fitted, buckled USCG-approved life jacket from launch to landing. Cold shock can begin immediately, so a stowed device cannot provide support at capsize. @X04,X02

baseline_exact: Any indoor CO alarm sound, headache/dizziness, or exhaust odor indoors requires shutting down and evacuating everyone to fresh air immediately plus calling 911. @C07,C06
a02_exact: If a CO alarm sounds or poisoning is suspected, get everyone to fresh outdoor air immediately and call 911 from outside. Do not delay to switch off the generator or investigate. @C07,C06

baseline_exact: Connect household appliances safely in ONLY one of two ways: plug individual appliances directly into the generator via intact heavy-duty outdoor-rated grounded cords, OR connect through a properly permitted transfer switch installed by a licensed electrician. @U02
a02_exact: Use appliance connections permitted by the specific generator manual and rated outdoor cords. Any connection to building wiring requires code-compliant transfer equipment installed by a licensed electrician. @U02

baseline_exact: NEVER plug a portable generator into a home wall outlet, laundry dryer outlet, or range receptacle using a double-male cord ("backfeeding" or "suicide cord")—backfeeding energizes exterior utility lines to deadly thousands of volts, killing utility linemen and bypassing breaker fire protection. @U02
a02_exact: Never connect a portable generator to a wall, dryer or range outlet. Backfeeding can energize utility lines and endanger utility workers and neighbors. @U02

baseline_exact: Any DIY panel tie-in, warm cord, tripped GFCI, or exposed live male prongs requires immediate shutdown and licensed electrical review. @U02
a02_exact: Do not touch exposed live parts or enter a hazardous area to stop equipment. Move away and contact emergency services or a licensed electrician as appropriate. @U02,U15

baseline_exact: Operate generators on a dry, level non-combustible outdoor surface shielded from direct rain or falling snow ONLY under a purpose-built open-sided canopy that preserves complete open-air ventilation on all sides—NEVER move a unit into a porch or garage to stay dry. @U15,C06
a02_exact: Keep a portable generator outdoors at the prescribed clearances, with exhaust pointed away from buildings. Use only equipment and weather protection the manufacturer permits in those conditions. Leave it off if it cannot stay dry without enclosing it. @U15,U02

baseline_exact: Wet energized outlets, leaking fuel lines, sparking cords, or indoor exhaust drift require immediate safe shutdown. @U15,U02
a02_exact: Keep away from wet or sparking equipment and leaking fuel. If exhaust enters a building or a CO alarm sounds, evacuate and call 911 before any equipment action. @U15,C07

baseline_exact: UL-listed packs + matched charger only | Hard surface clear of beds & exits | Swollen, hot or hissing -> stop & call 911
a02_exact: Compatible charger on safe surface | Recognize overheating or venting | Move people away and call for help

baseline_exact: Charge and store lithium batteries on hard, flat non-combustible surfaces well away from beds, couches, curtains, and primary room exit doors, and keep packs within manufacturer temperature limits (charging frozen lithium batteries below 32°F permanently damages cells and raises fire risk). @U09,U04
a02_exact: Follow the exact battery and charger temperature limits. Charge away from bedding and exits on a stable surface. Keep damaged or flood-exposed batteries out of service. @U09

baseline_exact: Stop using any battery pack IMMEDIATELY if it swells, hisses, smells sweet/chemical, overheats, leaks, or was dropped hard or submerged in floodwater; isolate safely outdoors away from structures if safe to move and follow local hazardous-waste disposal rules. @U09,U04
a02_exact: If a pack becomes unusually hot, hisses, vents, smokes or swells, move people away. Do not carry an actively failing pack through the home or attempt to disconnect it if that requires approaching it. @U09,U04

baseline_exact: Rotten-egg sulfur odor, hot bubbling battery case, sizzling terminals, or acid leak requires disconnecting safely if clear of sparks, ventilating, and evacuating. @U09,U11
a02_exact: If a battery case is hot, hissing, leaking or giving off an unusual odor, leave the area without operating nearby switches or disconnecting terminals. Seek emergency or qualified help from a safe location. @U09,U11

baseline_exact: Verify local code & exact indoor rating | Exact fuel only; fresh air + 3 ft clear | NEVER sleep with unvented fuel heat on
a02_exact: Confirm legal indoor-rated model | Follow its fuel and ventilation limits | Evacuate on suspected CO

baseline_exact: Sooty yellow flames, chemical odor, headache/drowsiness, or CO alarm requires turning the heater OFF immediately, exiting to fresh air, and calling 911 if symptomatic. @C07,U03
a02_exact: If a CO alarm sounds or poisoning is suspected, get everyone outside immediately and call 911. Do not stop to turn off the heater or wait for symptoms. @C07,U03

baseline_exact: Leave the building IMMEDIATELY with all occupants and pets, leaving doors open behind you—do NOT flip any light switches, unplug appliances, light matches, start cars in the driveway, or use landline/cell phones INSIDE the building (tiny electrical sparks ignite gas mixtures). @U11
a02_exact: Leave immediately with everyone who can exit safely. Do not operate lights, appliances, vehicles, garage controls or phones in the suspected leak area. Call 911 and the gas utility from a safe location. @U11

baseline_exact: If you smell leaking gas, hear hissing, or see structural/flood damage to gas piping and you can safely reach an exterior valve outside the building without entering gas fumes, follow your local gas utility's exact shutoff instructions (or evacuate first and let utility/fire crews shut it off). @U11
a02_exact: If you smell leaking gas, hear hissing or suspect damaged gas piping, leave immediately. Call 911 and the gas utility from a safe location. Leave valve manipulation and restoration to authorized responders. @U11

baseline_exact: Confirm household knows NEVER to restore shut-off gas service independently and keeps utility emergency numbers on paper. @U11,U14
a02_exact: Keep the utility emergency number available. Follow its instructions from a safe location and wait for clearance before returning. @U11

baseline_exact: Keep the affected faucet OPEN slightly while warming so melting water and steam can relieve pressure safely as ice loosens, and confirm someone stands ready at the main water shutoff in case the frozen pipe already cracked beneath the ice plug. @U10,U08
a02_exact: If an accessible pipe is frozen without signs of rupture, open the affected faucet before applying gentle heat. Know how to shut off the water if a leak develops. @U10

baseline_exact: Apply gentle indirect heat ONLY to accessible exposed pipe sections using a handheld hair dryer, warm soaked towels, or UL-listed electric heat tape installed strictly per label—working steadily from the open faucet back toward the frozen section. @U10,U03
a02_exact: Use warm towels or another method specifically advised by a plumber for the accessible pipe and site. Keep electrical devices away from wet surfaces. Never use a flame, torch or unapproved heater. @U10

baseline_exact: Kill heater power/gas & inlet FIRST | Flush sediment; draw clean tank reserve | NEVER drink boilers, pools or chem tanks
a02_exact: Verify prior potable supply and no advisory | Follow exact appliance instructions | Prefer stored potable water

baseline_exact: Before draining a household water heater for emergency water, FIRST turn off its electricity at the breaker (or shut off gas supply), close the cold-water inlet valve, open a hot tap upstairs to break vacuum, and draw from the bottom drain valve—flushing initial rusty sediment first and treating/boiling if any microbiological doubt exists. @U08,W02
a02_exact: Use tank water only if the supply was safe and the utility and heater manufacturer allow recovery. Have the safe shutdown, cooling and draining procedure ready in advance. Do not use a hot, damaged, pressurized or gas-leaking appliance. @U08,U11

baseline_exact: NEVER drink water from hydronic home heating radiators/boilers, waterbeds, swimming pools/spas (use strictly for non-potable flushing), or toilet tanks containing blue/chemical bowl cleaners or corroded parts. @U08,W01
a02_exact: Default to stored or officially supplied potable water when appliance instructions, system condition or advisory status are uncertain. @U08,D12

baseline_exact: Read the EXACT advisory tier issued by your local water utility or health department: **Boil Water** targets microbial risk (bring clear water to a rolling boil 1 minute; 3 minutes above 6,500 ft for drinking, brushing teeth, food washing, and infant formula). @W07,W02,W29
a02_exact: Read the active utility order. For a Boil Water advisory, use bottled water or follow the order’s exact boiling directions. Check the local instructions for infant feeding and every other use. @D12,W07

baseline_exact: Under a **Do Not Drink** advisory (chemical/algal/nitrate contamination), do NOT boil tap water—boiling does not remove chemicals and can concentrate or vaporize volatile toxins; use ONLY bottled or officially supplied safe water for ingestion and food prep. @W07,W01,D12
a02_exact: For a Do Not Drink advisory, use an approved alternate supply for ingestion and food preparation. Boiling does not remove hazardous chemicals. Use tap water for other tasks only if the advisory allows it. @D12,W01

baseline_exact: Remember that private well pumps stop instantly when electricity fails—once the small pressurized bladder tank empties (often just 5 to 15 gallons), EVERY household faucet and toilet stops flowing until power returns. @U06,U08,U01
a02_exact: A well may lose pressure or stop supplying water in an outage. Reserve capacity depends on the pressure system and settings. Follow the well contractor’s guidance on backup supply and tested operation. @U05,U06

baseline_exact: Switch OFF the dedicated well-pump breaker during flickering brownouts or prolonged outages until stable utility power or a properly licensed, adequately sized 240V transfer-switch generator circuit is ready (submersible pumps draw high startup surges that burn out under low voltage). @U06,U02,U01
a02_exact: Use stored potable water during a prolonged outage. Leave selection of a backup circuit and inspection after unstable power to licensed electrical and well professionals. @U02,U06

baseline_exact: NSF 42 = taste ONLY (not germs/lead) | Check exact NSF 53/58 named claim | Pitchers NEVER clear Boil Water notices
a02_exact: Identify specific contaminant and model claim | Follow utility and product instructions | Use approved safe supply for chemical advice

baseline_exact: Verify exact independent certification labels (NSF/ANSI or WQA) rather than marketing words: NSF 42 covers aesthetic chlorine/taste ONLY (NOT microbes or lead); NSF 53/58 require verifying the SPECIFIC named contaminant claim (such as cyst reduction, lead, or arsenic) on that exact cartridge. @W20,W21
a02_exact: Check the individual model’s listed reduction claim. NSF/ANSI 42 concerns aesthetic effects. NSF/ANSI 53 and 58 cover different systems and claims, and a standard number alone does not establish lead or cyst reduction. @W19,W20,W21

baseline_exact: Replace cartridges strictly on schedule (or immediately after any Boil Water / flood-contamination exposure) and protect wet cartridges from freezing, which cracks media silently. @W21,W28
a02_exact: Follow the product manual and utility instructions for replacement, flushing or reinstatement after contamination or freeze exposure. Sawyer’s wet hollow-fiber advice applies to its specified products. @W21,W28,D12

baseline_exact: Unknown certification, expired/clogged cartridges, freeze exposure, or active chemical/Boil Water advisories require switching to validated boiling or safe bottled water. @W20,W28,W07
a02_exact: For chemical or Do Not Use advisories, use an approved alternate supply. Boiling is an option only for a microbial advisory and only as the utility directs. @W01,W07,D12

baseline_exact: Mix household chlorine bleach STRICTLY with plain cool water per exact label directions—NEVER mix bleach with ammonia, window cleaners, urine/toilet cleaners, vinegar, lemon juice, or acidic rust/drain cleaners. @U13,M15
a02_exact: Use one cleaning product at a time and follow its label. Never mix bleach with other cleaners or disinfectants. @U19

baseline_exact: Recognize the exact chemical hazard: bleach + ammonia creates toxic chloramine gas, and bleach + acids (vinegar/toilet cleaner) creates lethal chlorine gas—both rapidly burn eyes, throats, and lungs even in open bathrooms. @U13,M15
a02_exact: If mixing has already released irritating fumes, move away to fresh air. For trouble breathing or collapse call 911 from safety. Contact Poison Control for exposure-specific advice. @U19,M15

baseline_exact: Ventilate rooms well when cleaning, wear gloves, keep all chemical bottles in original labeled containers high out of children's reach, and NEVER reuse empty drink bottles to store diluted bleach. @U13,M16
a02_exact: If indoor fumes are present, leave the area. Do not return to ventilate or clean until you have emergency or Poison Control guidance. @U19,M15

baseline_exact: Distinguish light greywater (clean dish-rinse or hand/bath water free of raw meat juices, bleach/harsh solvents, or fecal matter) from contaminated blackwater (toilet/diaper/raw-meat/sewage water)—ONLY light greywater is appropriate for emergency gravity-toilet bowl flushing. @U13,U07
a02_exact: Keep any non-potable water apart from drinking-water and food-preparation equipment. Do not use sewage-contaminated water or assume household wastewater is safe to reuse. @U07,U13

baseline_exact: Pour flush water briskly straight into the toilet BOWL (roughly 1 to 2 gallons triggers a standard gravity siphon flush) ONLY when you have verified the municipal sewer or gravity septic line is functioning and NOT flooded or pump-blocked. @U07,U13
a02_exact: Check local utility or health instructions before using any alternate flushing water. Do not add water to a failed, flooded or backing-up sewer or septic system. @U07,U13

baseline_exact: NEVER store greywater for more than 24 hours (bacteria multiply rapidly and turn foul), NEVER use greywater on edible garden leaves, and NEVER let greywater touch drinking-water jugs or kitchen food counters. @U13,P03,W06
a02_exact: Choose a locally approved sanitation alternative if wastewater service is uncertain. Avoid improvised connections between non-potable equipment and drinking water. @U07,U13

baseline_exact: NEVER wade into standing basement water until electricity to the basement (and entire flooded panel if submerged) is confirmed shut off by the utility or dry main switch, and check for gas odors before entering. @D05,U01,U11
a02_exact: Do not enter a flooded basement or touch switches in or near standing water. Call the utility or a licensed electrician to confirm isolation from a safe location. Leave immediately if you suspect a gas leak. @U20,U11

baseline_exact: Submerged electrical panel, gas odor, chest-deep water, structural wall cracking, or widespread black sewage contamination requires professional utility and remediation crews. @D05,U11
a02_exact: Re-enter only after applicable electrical, gas and structural clearance. Use professional cleanup for sewage or chemical contamination when safe control cannot be established. @U20,D05

baseline_exact: Strong gasoline/propane odor in a shed or garage requires ventilating immediately without touching electric switches, keeping flames away, and removing leaking cylinders outdoors. @U04,U11
a02_exact: For a strong fuel odor, active leak or hissing cylinder, leave the area. Avoid switches, engines and flames. Call the fire service or supplier from a safe location. Do not move a leaking cylinder yourself. @U11,U04

baseline_exact: Store potatoes in total darkness at 45–50°F to prevent toxic green solanine
a02_exact: Keep stored potatoes dark and discard green or bitter potatoes

baseline_exact: 100% total darkness + breathable bags | Hold 45–50°F (avoid below 40°F starch-sugar) | Discard heavily green/bitter solanine spuds
a02_exact: Store sound potatoes dark | Check for greening or strong sprouting | Discard suspect tubers

baseline_exact: Store cured potatoes in **100% TOTAL DARKNESS** inside breathable paper bags, burlap sacks, or covered slatted boxes—even dim basement daylight or electric bulbs trigger chlorophyll greening accompanied by toxic **solanine** (glycoalkaloids) beneath the peel. @P05,M15
a02_exact: Store sound potatoes in a cool, dark place with airflow using crop-specific Extension guidance. Light exposure can cause greening, which flags possible glycoalkaloid risk. @P05,P21

baseline_exact: Hold storage temperatures near 45–50°F (avoiding refrigerator temperatures below 40°F, which convert potato starch into sugar, turning cooked potatoes unpleasantly sweet and dark-browning when fried) with moderate-high humidity and good airflow. @P05
a02_exact: Discard green, bitter or heavily sprouted potatoes. Color is a warning cue rather than a measurement of toxin concentration. Do not taste a suspect potato to test it. @P21

baseline_exact: Inspect stored potatoes regularly—trim away small shallow sprouts and light green surface spots generously, and DISCARD heavily green, bitter-tasting, shriveled, or heavily sprouted potatoes completely (cooking does NOT destroy solanine!). @P05,M15
a02_exact: Check stored potatoes periodically and remove deteriorated ones. Discard green, bitter or strongly sprouted tubers without tasting them. @P21

baseline_exact: Confirm total darkness, breathable opaque bags (zero sealed sweaty plastic), 45–50°F target temp, and regular sprout/greening checks. @P05
a02_exact: Confirm darkness, suitable airflow and periodic inspection for deterioration. @P05,P21

baseline_exact: Heavily greened skins, bitter taste, or soft wet rot require discarding affected potatoes immediately rather than eating them. @P05,M15
a02_exact: Discard green, bitter, rotten or strongly sprouted potatoes. Do not assess safety by tasting. @P21

baseline_exact: Insert a clean food thermometer into the thickest portion of the food (away from bone, fat, or pan bottom) to confirm USDA safe minimum internal temperatures: **165°F** for all poultry and reheated leftovers/casseroles, **160°F** for ground beef/pork/lamb and egg dishes, and **145°F** (plus 3-minute rest) for whole cuts of beef, pork, veal, lamb, and fish (145°F). @F02
a02_exact: Use a food thermometer and the USDA chart. The minimum is 165°F for poultry and reheated leftovers or casseroles, 160°F for ground beef, pork, veal or lamb and egg dishes, and 145°F plus a three-minute rest for whole cuts of beef, pork, veal or lamb. Fish is a separate 145°F entry. @F03

baseline_exact: For **refrigerated** foods held above 40°F for OVER 2 hours: DISCARD meat, poultry, fish, eggs, soft cheeses, milk, cut melons/tomatoes/leafy greens, cooked pasta/rice/leftovers, and opened mayo/creamy dressings; items like hard cheeses, uncut whole produce, butter, peanut butter, jams, and vinegar condiments are generally listed as keepable per the official chart. @F04,P17
a02_exact: Use the per-food refrigerated discard chart after an outage. An unopened refrigerator gives about four hours of cold holding. Discard vulnerable foods at the applicable time and temperature limit or when the cold history is unknown. @F04,P17

baseline_exact: For **frozen** foods: you may safely refreeze or cook foods that STILL contain visible ice crystals OR measure **40°F or below** on a food/appliance thermometer (expecting minor texture/quality softening); discard thawed meat/poultry/seafood/egg/dairy dishes held above 40°F over 2 hours. @F05,P17
a02_exact: For frozen items, check the separate FDA/USDA freezer chart. Ice crystals or a measured 40°F or below are relevant, but some categories have specific discard rules. @F04,P17

baseline_exact: When temperature history is unknown or exceeds 40°F for >2 hours on high-risk perishables, discard cleanly ("When in doubt, throw it out"). @F04,P17
a02_exact: If you cannot establish which chart row applies or whether temperature control held, discard the suspect food. Do not taste it. @F04,P17

baseline_exact: Classify every food strictly by the **pH 4.6** botulism boundary: **Low-acid foods (pH > 4.6)** include ALL meats, poultry, seafood, stocks, soups, beans, corn, carrots, potatoes, green beans, squash, and vegetable mixes—these MUST be processed strictly in a **PRESSURE CANNER** reaching 240°F+ to destroy heat-resistant C. botulinum spores. @P07,F06
a02_exact: Use only tested USDA/NCHFP recipes. Low-acid products such as plain vegetables, meat and poultry require a validated pressure-canning recipe with the specified equipment and conditions. @P06,P07

baseline_exact: **High-acid foods (pH ≤ 4.6)** include most fruits, tested fruit jams/jellies, tested fermented sauerkraut, tested vinegar pickles, and properly acidified tomatoes—these may be processed in a boiling-water canner (212°F at sea level) strictly per a tested recipe. @P08,F06
a02_exact: Use boiling-water canning for high-acid or properly acidified products only when the exact tested recipe calls for it. A measured pH alone does not create a validated process. @P06,P08

baseline_exact: Recognize that boiling water at 212°F NEVER kills C. botulinum spores no matter how many hours you boil a jar—in an oxygen-free sealed low-acid jar at room temperature, surviving spores germinate and produce the most potent biological toxin known. @P07,P10
a02_exact: An ordinary boiling-water bath does not provide a validated process for low-acid products. If no tested recipe exists, choose safe refrigeration or a tested alternate preservation method. @P06,P07

baseline_exact: Acidify home-canned tomatoes strictly with bottled lemon juice or citric acid
a02_exact: Acidify home-canned tomatoes using the exact tested recipe

baseline_exact: Acidify EVERY jar of home-canned tomatoes—whether processed in a boiling-water canner OR a pressure canner—using USDA's exact standardized measure (typically 1 tablespoon bottled lemon juice or ¼ teaspoon citric acid per pint; 2 tablespoons bottled lemon juice or ½ teaspoon citric acid per quart, per the exact tested recipe). @P08,P06
a02_exact: For whole, crushed or juiced tomatoes, use a tested recipe and its prescribed acid and jar size. NCHFP lists specific bottled lemon juice, citric acid and 5% vinegar options for its applicable procedures. They are not interchangeable by volume. @P08,P22

baseline_exact: Use **BOTTLED lemon juice** (standardized acidity) or dry citric acid—NEVER substitute fresh-squeezed lemons or limes whose natural acidity varies unpredictably by cultivar and ripeness, and never skip acid because a tomato variety "tastes tart." @P08
a02_exact: Keep the recipe’s acid step even if it offers a pressure-canning option. Do not generalize these directions to salsa, mixed products or another jar size. @P22,P06

baseline_exact: Select ONLY firm, sound, vine-ripened tomatoes—NEVER can tomatoes from dead, frost-killed vines (which drop sharply in acidity) or heavily bruised/decayed fruit. @P08,P04
a02_exact: Use sound fruit and reject fruit from dead or frost-killed vines for canning. Follow all preparation and processing conditions in the same tested recipe. @P22

baseline_exact: Confirm firm healthy pre-frost tomatoes, standardized bottled lemon juice/citric acid added directly per jar, and tested USDA processing schedule followed. @P08,P06
a02_exact: Confirm the fruit, jar size, acid and complete processing schedule match one tested recipe. @P22

baseline_exact: Overripe soft tomatoes, frost-killed vine tomatoes, or missing standardized acid require freezing instead of home canning. @P08,P12
a02_exact: If the tomato source, acid option or processing schedule fails the tested conditions, do not can that batch. @P22

baseline_exact: Use an atmospheric-steam canner STRICTLY for **high-acid tested boiling-water recipes (pH ≤ 4.6)**—an atmospheric steam canner is NOT pressurized and NEVER replaces a pressure canner for meats, vegetables, or low-acid foods. @P08,P07
a02_exact: Use atmospheric steam canning only for an applicable high-acid or acidified tested recipe and compatible equipment. It cannot replace pressure canning for low-acid foods. @P25

baseline_exact: Enforce the mandatory **45-minute maximum processing time cap** (INCLUDING all altitude time adjustments!)—steam canners hold shallow base water that can boil dry beyond 45 minutes, silently dropping chamber temperature below safe pasteurization levels. @P08
a02_exact: Follow the tested steam-canning procedure. The total processing time, including elevation adjustment, must be 45 minutes or less. @P25

baseline_exact: Vent until pure steam flows steadily and the dome gauge confirms full boiling temperature for your elevation before starting the timer, keep heat steady without boiling dry, and never open the dome early. @P08,P14
a02_exact: Vent and monitor steam temperature according to the validated instructions and exact equipment. Maintain these conditions without running dry. @P25

baseline_exact: Confirm high-acid recipe ONLY, total altitude-adjusted time ≤45 minutes, full pure steam verified, and base water never boils dry. @P08,P14
a02_exact: Confirm the tested recipe, compatible equipment and altitude-adjusted time within the 45-minute limit. @P25

baseline_exact: Any recipe exceeding 45 total minutes (with altitude) or any low-acid food requires switching to a deep boiling-water or pressure canner respectively. @P08,P07
a02_exact: If the recipe, elevation-adjusted time or equipment fails the validated conditions, select the correct tested procedure instead. @P25,P07

baseline_exact: Purge cold insulating air pockets completely from the pressure canner so internal temperature truly reaches 240°F+ across all jars.
a02_exact: Identify the open-vent stage, then start timing only at the tested target pressure for the recipe, gauge and elevation.

baseline_exact: All low-acid home canning (meats, poultry, stocks, beans, vegetables, tested soups) in a validated stovetop dial- or weighted-gauge pressure canner.
a02_exact: A tested pressure-canning recipe and compatible model. The same operating setting does not apply to every product or site.

baseline_exact: Clear vent pipe -> 10 MIN FULL STEAM VENT | Apply weight -> reach altitude-adjusted PSI | Hold steady PSI full time; avoid swings
a02_exact: Ten minutes of continuous steam venting | Recipe-specific gauge and elevation values | Maintain the target for the specified time

baseline_exact: System boundary pressure-canner cutaway illustrating 10-minute air-purge steam funnel, locked lid/gasket, dial/weighted gauge, and 240°F+ jar zone. Conceptual, not to scale.
a02_exact: Conceptual cross-section of steam escaping through the open lid vent before the canner pressurizes. The tested recipe and manufacturer instructions control water depth, pressure and loading.

baseline_exact: Inspect the rubber lid gasket, safety overpressure plug, and open vent pipe (look cleanly through the pipe toward light!) before every use, add the manufacturer-specified 2 to 3 inches of hot water over the bottom rack, lock the lid, and leave the vent weight OFF. @P07
a02_exact: Inspect the gasket, vent and safety components per the model manual. Use the tested recipe and instructions for the rack, water depth and loading. Leave the vent open for the venting step. @P07

baseline_exact: Heat on high until a **STRONG, CONTINUOUS FUNNEL OF STEAM** flows from the open vent pipe, then time a **FULL 10 MINUTES OF STEADY VENTING** BEFORE placing the counterweight/petcock on—skipping the 10-minute vent traps cool air pockets inside the pot so the gauge reads target PSI while actual jar temperatures stay fatally low! @P07
a02_exact: Time ten minutes of continuous steam from the open vent. Then close the petcock or place the regulator as the manual specifies. @P07

baseline_exact: Once pressurized cleanly to exact altitude-adjusted PSI (e.g., 11 PSI dial / 10 PSI weighted at ≤1,000 ft, stepped up above 1,000 ft per USDA tables), start the exact recipe timer and hold steady pressure without wild burner swings (which cause jar liquid siphoning). @P07,P14
a02_exact: Use the tested recipe’s pressure for the actual site elevation and gauge type. Start the process time only at target pressure and maintain it throughout. @P07,P14

baseline_exact: Do NOT try to guess "just add 10 extra minutes"—cumulative heat transfer to the geometric center of sealed jars is non-linear and only restarting the full validated cycle guarantees safety. @P07,P06
a02_exact: Do not add an arbitrary number of minutes. If pressure falls below the recipe target, restore it and restart the full time following the tested method. For process deviations or uncertainty about the batch, consult Extension before using it. @P07,P06

baseline_exact: Apply the exact USDA altitude adjustment for your equipment: for **boiling-water canning**, add extra processing minutes per the recipe's elevation bracket (1,001–3,000 ft, 3,001–6,000 ft, etc.); for **pressure canning**, INCREASE target pressure (e.g., dial gauge moves from 11 PSI to 12 PSI at 2,001–4,000 ft; weighted gauge steps straight from 10 PSI to **15 PSI** above 1,000 ft!). @P14,P07,F07
a02_exact: Use the elevation column of the exact tested recipe for the specified equipment. Water-bath times and pressure-canner settings are different controls. Do not transfer a pressure value between a dial and weighted gauge. @P07,P14

baseline_exact: After 12 to 24 hours of undisturbed cooling, remove ALL metal screw bands cleanly and test every flat lid: a properly sealed lid curves slightly **CONCAVE (downward)** at the center, does NOT flex or pop up/down when pressed gently, and holds firmly when lifted carefully by the lid rim edges just an inch above the towel. @P09
a02_exact: After 12–24 hours of undisturbed cooling, remove bands and check for a firm seal by an NCHFP method. A seal check cannot verify a recipe or processing schedule. @P09,P10

baseline_exact: If ANY jar fails to seal within 24 hours of processing, immediately choose one of three safe NCHFP options: **refrigerate and eat promptly**, **freeze** in freezer-safe containers, OR **reprocess the ENTIRE full time** using a clean inspected jar rim and a brand-new flat lid within 24 hours. @P09,P10
a02_exact: For a freshly unsealed jar, reprocess only if the original method and the corrective procedure meet Extension conditions. Consult the exact instructions for refrigeration, freezing or reprocessing. @P09,P10

baseline_exact: Unsealed jars discovered MORE than 24 hours after processing must be treated as spoiled and discarded safely without tasting. @P10
a02_exact: An unsealed jar from a correctly processed batch has a narrow reprocessing window under the tested instructions. If the original process was wrong, unknown, or shows spoilage, do not treat a later seal as clearance. @P09,P10

baseline_exact: Check concave seal & clean jar exterior | Look for spurting, gas bubbles, cloud or mold | Suspect jar -> ZERO tasting; isolate NOW
a02_exact: Check the sealed container and recipe record | Isolate defects or uncertain process | Do not open or taste for diagnosis

baseline_exact: Failure-mode jar-inspection guide mapping external seal/rust cues, opening-spurt cues, and internal bubble/mold flags to strict zero-taste isolation. Conceptual, not to scale.
a02_exact: Failure-mode diagram showing external container defects and uncertain processing as reasons to keep a suspect jar closed and seek disposal guidance.

baseline_exact: Inspect EVERY jar BEFORE opening: confirm the lid is still tightly **CONCAVE** and pulls a crisp inward vacuum hiss (NEVER an outward spurt or fizz!) when opened, with zero dried food streaks down the glass exterior and zero rust holes. @P10,P09
a02_exact: Check the intact container and processing record before opening. Keep a suspect jar closed and isolated. A concave lid or vacuum sound cannot verify safety. @P10,P06

baseline_exact: Inspect jar contents carefully through the glass before and right after opening for rising gas bubbles, unexpected cloudiness/sediment, mold fuzz under the lid, mushy slimy texture, or sour/putrid off-odor. @P10
a02_exact: Look for unusual leakage, bulging, broken seal or visible changes without opening a suspect jar or sniffing its contents. Follow official isolation and disposal instructions. @P10

baseline_exact: Confirm intact concave seal, normal clear appearance/odor, zero mold/spurting, and confirmed tested USDA process lineage before serving. @P10,P06
a02_exact: Confirm the tested process record and container condition. Never use smell, taste or the sound of a lid as safety clearance. @P10,P06

baseline_exact: Detoxify and dispose of suspect botulism jars safely per NCHFP rules
a02_exact: Isolate suspect canned food and follow official disposal guidance

baseline_exact: ZERO tasting; never sink or compost dump | Sealed suspect -> double-bag locked trash | Opened/leaking -> 30 m submerged boil detox
a02_exact: Isolate suspect jar and prevent exposure | Use official disposal instructions | Call for help if exposure is suspected

baseline_exact: Branch decision tree separating unopened double-bag trash disposal from opened/leaking 30-minute submerged boil detoxification and 911 emergency exposure care. Conceptual, not to scale.
a02_exact: Decision schematic for isolating suspect food, reporting symptoms and using official disposal instructions.

baseline_exact: NEVER taste a suspect jar, dump it down a sink disposal, or toss it into compost or yards where pets or wildlife can ingest fatal botulinum toxin. @P10
a02_exact: Keep suspect jars away from people and animals. Never taste the contents or open a sealed suspect container to inspect it. @P10

baseline_exact: If a suspect low-acid jar is STILL SEALED/UNOPENED, carefully double-bag it padded in cardboard inside locked household landfill trash out of reach of children and animals, then wash hands thoroughly. @P10
a02_exact: Get the current NCHFP or public-health disposal directions. Identify whether the container is sealed, open or leaking and whether anyone ate the food. Keep children and pets out of the area. @P10

baseline_exact: If LEAKING or ALREADY OPENED, wear gloves and follow NCHFP detoxification: submerge jar, lid, and contents under 1+ inch of water in a large covered pot, boil vigorously 30 FULL MINUTES, cool, then bag/trash cleanly; wipe spills with 1:5 bleach-water for 30 minutes (no ammonia/acid). @P10,U13
a02_exact: For a suspected exposure, call Poison Control or public health promptly. Trouble swallowing or breathing, double vision or progressive weakness after eating suspect food requires emergency medical care. Keep the container isolated and follow health authorities’ instructions. @M15,P23

baseline_exact: Confirm zero tasting, zero sink/compost dumping, and exact NCHFP unopened-trash OR 30-minute boil detoxification applied. @P10
a02_exact: Confirm no tasting, no access by pets or children, and receipt of official handling or disposal directions. @P10

baseline_exact: Anyone who tasted suspect low-acid food requires calling 911 IMMEDIATELY for hospital antitoxin (save jar safely for public-health testing). @P10,M15,T02
a02_exact: For a leaking container, contaminated surface or symptomatic exposure, avoid handling and seek public-health or emergency guidance. @P10,P23

baseline_exact: Trim away ALL visible fat completely before slicing lean meat into uniform thin strips (≤¼ inch thick)—fat does NOT dry and turns rancid quickly in storage. @P11,P18
a02_exact: Use one tested jerky protocol. For the USDA FSIS method, heat meat to 160°F (71°C) and poultry to 165°F (74°C) before dehydrating, and confirm the temperature in several pieces with a food thermometer. @P24

baseline_exact: Follow NCHFP's mandatory **pathogen-kill heating step** because standard 130–140°F dehydrator air is too cool to destroy E. coli and Salmonella reliably: EITHER heat meat strips in boiling marinade/brine BEFORE drying to an internal temperature of **160°F for red meat / 165°F for poultry** verified by thermometer, OR heat finished oven-baked/dehydrated strips in a 275°F oven for 10 minutes to reach 160°F/165°F internal temperature per Extension guidelines. @P11,F02
a02_exact: Use controlled drying equipment at the temperature and conditions specified in that same procedure. Texture alone cannot demonstrate adequate initial heating. @P24

baseline_exact: Dry pre-heated strips rapidly at 130–140°F+ until leathery (cracks when bent without snapping completely), blot any surface oil cleanly with paper towels, and store refrigerated or frozen for best safety/shelf life rather than assuming indefinite warm-room storage. @P11,P18
a02_exact: Follow the same tested procedure for endpoint, packaging and storage. Avoid claiming room-temperature safety if an equipment or process condition cannot be verified. @P24

baseline_exact: Unheated raw-dried meat jerky, tacky damp centers, or oily rancid odor must be discarded cleanly. @P11
a02_exact: If you cannot verify the initial heating or the specified drying conditions, do not use the batch as shelf-stable food. @P24

baseline_exact: Check active ferments regularly during the multi-week cycle: healthy lacto-fermentation smells crisply sour/tangy with clear or slightly cloudy bubbling brine and firm crisp vegetables completely beneath the liquid line. @P13
a02_exact: Use the spoilage and storage criteria from the exact tested ferment. If mold, abnormal odor or texture, or process deviation raises doubt, stop and seek Extension advice. Never taste to check safety. @P13,P10

baseline_exact: For formula-fed infants, stock **ready-to-feed liquid infant formula** (requires zero mixing water during water outages or Boil Water advisories!) alongside clean disposable nipples/bottles—if powdered formula is used during a water advisory, mix strictly with bottled or properly boiled-and-cooled safe water per CDC rules. @P15,W29
a02_exact: Prefer ready-to-feed formula during outages, especially for infants under two months, born prematurely or with weakened immune systems. If only powder is available, follow current CDC and local instructions for the infant and water advisory. Powder is not sterile. @P26,W29

baseline_exact: Call 911 with your highway/milepost/GPS location, tie a bright cloth to the antenna or top of a rolled-up window, turn on the interior dome light at night when running briefly, and huddle occupants together under winter blankets/layers. @E14,T06
a02_exact: When safely stranded outside, NWS describes running the engine for about ten minutes each hour if the tailpipe is clear and a window is open slightly. Check conditions first. Do not run with blocked exhaust or suspected CO. @D19,C07

baseline_exact: Any exhaust odor, headache, drowsiness, or rapidly drifting snow sealing the undercarriage requires shutting off the engine immediately and relying on dry layered insulation. @E14,C07
a02_exact: If the exhaust cannot be kept clear, do not run the engine. If CO is suspected, turn it off only if this does not delay reaching fresh air and contacting 911. Tell dispatch about any unsafe conditions outside the vehicle. @D19,C07

baseline_exact: If caught inside a vehicle with a tornado visibly approaching and NO sturdy building reachable: either drive smoothly at right angles away from the tornado path if traffic/roads allow, OR pull safely off the road, stay buckled inside the vehicle with head below window level covered by coats/arms, or lie flat in a low ditch ONLY if well lower than the road and free of flash-flood water (protecting head/neck). @D03,E17
a02_exact: If the nearest sturdy shelter is unreachable, follow local warnings and use last-resort protection. NWS guidance distinguishes a belted vehicle with head below windows from a lower spot on foot only when it is safely reachable and free of flood danger. Do not try to judge the tornado’s course and race it. @D03,E17

baseline_exact: Respect proven floodwater force thresholds: just **6 inches** of fast-moving water can knock a healthy adult off their feet, **12 inches** of rushing water floats and sweeps away most passenger cars, and **18 to 24 inches** carries away heavy SUVs and pickup trucks effortlessly. @D05,T07,N10
a02_exact: NWS depth examples illustrate how little moving water can knock people down or sweep away cars. They are warnings, not decision thresholds. Flooded roads can conceal damaged pavement or dangerous current. @D05,T16

baseline_exact: ANY water covering a roadway where pavement markings and roadbed stability cannot be verified is an automatic turnaround stop. @D05,N10
a02_exact: Turn around at any flooded roadway or barricade. Use an official open route or wait on safe high ground. @D05,T16

baseline_exact: Escape a stalled or flooded vehicle safely without wading into swift current
a02_exact: Avoid flooded roads and call for rescue if trapped in a vehicle

baseline_exact: Best cure: NEVER enter flooded roads | Stalled in rising water -> windows open NOW | Climb to high ground or roof + call 911
a02_exact: Do not enter floodwater | If trapped, give 911 the exact location and conditions | Follow rescue instructions

baseline_exact: Four-step flooded-vehicle escape plate showing early turnaround prevention, immediate window opening, safe high-ground/roof climb, and 911 swift-water call. Conceptual, not to scale.
a02_exact: Decision schematic showing prevention, reporting and emergency rescue. No vehicle exit mechanism is prescribed.

baseline_exact: If a vehicle stalls in rising water on a flooded road, act BEFORE water pressure pins car doors shut: **unbuckle, lower windows early** while battery power still operates, abandon the car ONLY if safe shallow non-rushing ground is immediately reachable—otherwise climb straight onto the **ROOF of the vehicle** and call 911 immediately rather than trying to wade through fast deep current. @D05,N10
a02_exact: If floodwater is rising around a vehicle, call 911 as soon as you can without delaying immediate escape from a sinking vehicle. Give the location, occupants and water conditions. @D05,T02

baseline_exact: If water rapidly rises inside a submerged vehicle and doors will not open against outside water pressure, exit through an open or broken **SIDE window** (never kick a laminated windshield—it will not shatter out cleanly; strike the corner of tempered side glass if a rescue tool is carried). @D05,ED
a02_exact: If safe high ground is immediately accessible without entering moving water, move to it. Otherwise tell dispatch what exits and hazards you can see and follow rescue instructions. A stalled vehicle in fast current is a specialist-rescue situation. @D05,T16

baseline_exact: Never stay trapped inside a sinking vehicle trying to restart a flooded engine or call a tow truck while water climbs past the floorboards. @D05
a02_exact: Never enter floodwater to follow another vehicle or save property. Do not depend on window glass type, vehicle stability or a predicted water depth. @D05,T16

baseline_exact: Confirm vehicle occupants know never to drive into floodwater first, and if suddenly engulfed, exit windows early to high ground or vehicle roof + 911. @D05,N10
a02_exact: Confirm the group knows the turnaround rule and how to report a trapped vehicle without entering the water as a bystander. @D05,T16,ED

baseline_exact: Fast-moving chest-deep current around a trapped car prohibits wading—hold on the vehicle roof and summon swift-water 911 rescue. @D05
a02_exact: Rising or fast-moving water, structural uncertainty or a submerged route requires immediate emergency help. @D05,T02

baseline_exact: Follow official three-tier **Ready – Set – Go** wildfire posture: **READY** (year-round defensible space, go-bags, two routes mapped), **SET** (fire nearby/Advisory: load go-bags, prescriptions, IDs, and pets into the car parked FACING OUTWARD toward the road with full fuel tank, dress in cotton/wool long sleeves and sturdy boots, monitor alerts nonstop), and **GO** (mandatory/voluntary order: leave IMMEDIATELY!). @D08,C19,D14
a02_exact: Learn the evacuation terms your locality uses before fire season. Stage documents, medications, pets and an accessible route early. Leave promptly when directed, using official routes. @D08,D14

baseline_exact: Drive with headlights ON (low beams in thick smoke), windows rolled tightly UP, and vehicle cabin air set strictly to **RECIRCULATE** (blocking outside smoke and embers from entering cabin vents), moving calmly with traffic flow along **official law-enforcement evacuation routes**. @D08,D14,D06
a02_exact: Leave early using official open routes. Follow responders’ guidance if smoke cuts visibility. Closed windows and recirculation may reduce particles briefly, but they do not make a vehicle safe in smoke, fire or carbon monoxide. @D06,D08

baseline_exact: Smoke + no AC + heat wave = lethal trap | Heat stroke kills faster -> prioritize cooling | Relocate early to AC clean-air center
a02_exact: Smoke and indoor heat both matter | Seek cool cleaner air before loss of protection | 911 and active cooling for heat-stroke signs

baseline_exact: Recognize the compound hazard trap: sealing windows tightly against smoke inside a home WITHOUT air conditioning causes indoor heat to climb to life-threatening heat-stroke levels within hours—**acute heat stroke kills much faster than brief moderate smoke exposure**. @D07,D09
a02_exact: Closed windows may reduce smoke exposure while indoor heat increases. Check both conditions and look for cooled, cleaner-air shelter before a power or cooling failure occurs. @D06,D20

baseline_exact: If using a window or portable air conditioner during smoke, verify it is set to **RECIRCULATE** indoor air (avoid single-hose portable AC units or evaporative swamp coolers that pull smokey outdoor air directly inside unless paired with HEPA filtration, and watch indoor thermometer continuously). @D07,D09
a02_exact: Use recirculation when available and compatible with the cooling equipment. If the dwelling cannot stay cool and cleaner than outside, relocate when safe and follow local alerts. @D07,D20

baseline_exact: Dangerous indoor heat buildup overrides window-sealing rules—relocate immediately to an air-conditioned clean-air space or summon 911 for heat-illness symptoms. @D07,D09,T09
a02_exact: If confusion, collapse or other signs of heat stroke occur, call 911 and begin dispatcher-guided cooling. Otherwise move early to safely accessible cleaner, cooled shelter. @D20,T09

baseline_exact: Manage home cooling during extreme heat waves and recognize electric-fan limits
a02_exact: Manage home cooling and follow the CDC indoor fan limit

baseline_exact: Fans FAIL to prevent heat stroke >~95°F | Block south/west sun; cool wet cloths/bath | Move vulnerable people to AC cooling center
a02_exact: Monitor indoor heat | CDC fan advice applies below 90°F | Use safer cooled shelter if heat rises

baseline_exact: Correct versus incorrect extreme-heat cooling contrasting cool basements, wet cloths, and AC cooling centers against relying on fans in >95°F indoor heat. Conceptual, not to scale.
a02_exact: Comparison of cooled shelter and the CDC indoor fan limit. The figure is not a clinical threshold.

baseline_exact: Understand the critical CDC/FEMA **electric fan limit**: electric fans move air to evaporate sweat in moderate heat, BUT when indoor air climbs into extreme heat ranges (above roughly **95°F**) with high humidity, blowing superheated air directly onto skin can actually **INCREASE** heat gain rather than cool the body—never rely on fans as your primary heat-wave defense! @D09,E08
a02_exact: CDC recommends fans only when indoor temperatures are below 90°F (32°C). In hotter rooms, use a cooler location or air conditioning rather than relying on a fan for protection. @D21

baseline_exact: During summer outages or non-AC heat waves, move to the coolest lowest shaded floor (such as a dry basement), block direct sunlight on south/west glass with curtains or reflective shades, take cool showers/baths or drape cool damp cloths across neck, wrists, and torso, and eat light no-cook meals. @D09,E19
