a02_exact: Choose the coolest safe location and use cool showers or wet cloths if available. Avoid a basement if flood, gas or utility hazards make it unsafe. @D21,D05,U11

baseline_exact: Confirm real indoor temperature measured, fans NOT relied upon above ~95°F, cool-cloth/basement cooling used, and AC shelter plan active. @D09
a02_exact: Check indoor heat independently and confirm a reachable cooled alternative. Do not rely on a fan at 90°F or above. @D21,ED

baseline_exact: Indoor air climbing past safe comfort toward 90–95°F without AC requires moving vulnerable occupants immediately to public air-conditioned spaces. @D09,U17
a02_exact: If you cannot keep vulnerable people cool, move early to a cooled safe location. Call 911 for confusion or collapse in heat. @D21,T09

baseline_exact: Start continuous rapid cooling IMMEDIATELY while awaiting the ambulance: immerse trunk/limbs in cold water if safely available (keeping airway supported above water), OR douse continuously with cold water and cold wet sheets/towels over neck, armpits, groin, and chest while fanning aggressively. @T09,T05
a02_exact: Start cooling while help is on the way. Move to shade or a cooler place when safe and cool the skin with water and airflow. Discuss immersion with dispatch, particularly when airway protection, patient type or available help is uncertain. @T09,M27

baseline_exact: Keep bystanders clear for airflow, do NOT force drinks into a confused or drowsy person's mouth, and follow live 911 dispatcher guidance until EMS transports the patient to an emergency department. @T09,M05
a02_exact: Give nothing by mouth to a confused or drowsy person. Monitor breathing and follow 911 instructions until EMS arrives. @T09,M27

baseline_exact: Confirm the EXACT official advisory tier from your water utility or health department before touching tap water: **Boil Water** (microbial risk → clear water rolling boil 1 min; 3 min above 6,500 ft), **Do Not Drink** (chemical/algal risk → NEVER boil; bottled/supplied water ONLY), or **Do Not Use** (severe hazard → zero skin/bath/dish/drinking contact). @D12,W07,W02
a02_exact: Read the exact active water advisory. Be clear whether it directs a Boil Water, Do Not Drink or Do Not Use response. Confirm which activities the local order permits. @D12,W07

baseline_exact: Immediately switch OFF automatic refrigerator icemakers and water dispensers, dump suspect ice, use safe bottled/boiled-and-cooled water for brushing teeth, washing ready-to-eat produce, and mixing infant formula, and rely on disposable plates to stretch drinking reserves. @D12,W29,U13
a02_exact: Follow the active advisory for icemakers, brushing teeth, preparing food and infant feeding. Use an approved alternative supply when required. Boiling is an option only for a microbial advisory and only as directed. @D12,W01,W07

baseline_exact: Wait for formal laboratory-tested utility clearance before flushing cold taps, replacing exposed inline carbon filters, and restoring normal tap use. @D12,W07
a02_exact: Wait for the local authority to lift the advisory and follow its flushing, appliance and filter directions. @D12,W21

baseline_exact: Interior windowless/minimal-window room, HVAC/fan shutoff access, pre-cut plastic sheeting + duct tape (ONLY when officially directed), and NOAA/local radio.
a02_exact: A reliable local alert channel and the shelter-in-place supplies recommended by local authorities.

baseline_exact: Move in NOW; lock ALL doors & windows | Shut OFF HVAC, fans & vents (zero intake) | Above-ground room; unseal fast on all-clear
a02_exact: Follow official shelter or evacuation instructions | Use the directed room and ventilation steps | Follow all-clear or revised order

baseline_exact: System boundary hazmat cutaway showing locked exterior envelope, HVAC/exhaust fans switched OFF, above-ground interior refuge, and heavy-gas basement avoidance. Conceptual, not to scale.
a02_exact: External chemical release decision schematic. Room, duration and ventilation depend on official direction.

baseline_exact: Move EVERY person and pet indoors IMMEDIATELY on a hazmat Shelter-in-Place alert, close and lock ALL exterior doors and windows, and **SHUT OFF ALL HVAC SYSTEMS, FURNACES, AIR CONDITIONERS, BATHROOM/KITCHEN EXHAUST FANS, AND FIREPLACE DAMPERS** so mechanical fans do NOT suck outside chemical vapors indoors. @D15,E24
a02_exact: When local officials direct chemical shelter-in-place, go indoors and follow their directions for windows, doors and shutting off outside-air systems. Keep an alert channel active. @D15

baseline_exact: Move to an interior room (preferably ABOVE ground level, because many heavy industrial gases like chlorine or anhydrous ammonia sink into basements and low spots!), and seal door/window/vent gaps temporarily with plastic sheeting and duct tape **ONLY when local authorities specifically instruct sealing**. @D15,E24
a02_exact: Use the interior room and temporary sealing measures specified by authorities. Room location depends on the release, building and local instructions. Do not infer a safe floor from the chemical name or odor. @D15

baseline_exact: Monitor official emergency broadcasts continuously and **UNSEAL AND VENTILATE PROMPTLY** the moment officials announce the all-clear—short-term sealed rooms build up carbon dioxide over hours and are strictly temporary (typically a few hours, NOT multi-day living!). @D15,E24
a02_exact: Stay alert for changes. Follow official all-clear instructions on when to leave, ventilate or evacuate. A gas leak or carbon monoxide alarm inside the dwelling calls for getting out and calling 911 from safety. @D15,U11,C07

baseline_exact: Strong chemical odor, burning eyes/throat inside a sealed room, or an official upgrade to Evacuation requires immediate action per fire/hazmat responders and 911. @D15,M15
a02_exact: An official evacuation order, fire or internal gas or CO hazard overrides a generic stay-put rule. Use the safest available exit and follow dispatch. @D15,U11,C07

baseline_exact: Match indoor air defense strictly to the hazard: for **wildfire smoke** (multi-day PM2.5 particles), keep windows closed with HVAC on RECIRCULATE and a non-ozone portable **HEPA air cleaner** running (relocating to AC if heat spikes); for an **outdoor chemical/hazmat plume** (short-term gas/vapor), switch **ALL HVAC and exhaust fans OFF** and seal an above-ground room ONLY per official order (HEPA does NOT stop toxic gases!). @D07,D06,D15
a02_exact: For wildfire particles use cleaner indoor air and filtered recirculation if the building can stay cool. Relocate early if it cannot. For an external chemical release follow specific directions on room and ventilation controls. @D07,D15,D20

baseline_exact: Contrast both with **INDOOR gas leak, carbon monoxide alarm, or advancing flames**, where staying inside is LETHAL—evacuate IMMEDIATELY into clean open outdoor air and move upwind/away. @U11,C07,D08
a02_exact: HEPA filters remove particles. They do not make a room safe from all chemicals or carbon monoxide. Follow emergency directions rather than substituting one shelter method for another. @D07,D15,C07

baseline_exact: Written household headcount/buddy list, school/daycare emergency cards, and Red Cross Safe & Well / out-of-area relay contact.
a02_exact: Written household headcount and buddy list, school/daycare emergency cards, and the locally designated reunification contact.

baseline_exact: Check in formally at the shelter registration desk upon arrival AND update your status through official channels (such as Red Cross Safe & Well and your out-of-area family relay) so anxious relatives and SAR teams know you are safe. @D14,T11
a02_exact: Check in through the shelter’s locally designated process and let your out-of-area contact know where you are if safe. Ask staff about accessibility and reunification support. @D14,T10

baseline_exact: Commit in advance to FIVE objective red lines where staying home STOPS immediately: **1)** acute medical red flag, worsening chronic illness, or under 48 hours of critical prescriptions/medical power; **2)** uncontrolled indoor freezing cold or extreme >90–95°F un-cooled heat; **3)** persistent CO alarm, gas leak, structural damage, or sewage/hazmat hazard; **4)** drinking water under 48 hours with zero safe resupply; **5)** official mandatory evacuation order. @U17,D18,D14,T10
a02_exact: Recognize immediate exit or emergency triggers: serious illness, fire, a suspected internal gas leak, a CO alarm, or an official evacuation order. Contact 911 from safety. For dwindling medication or medical power, use a reserve margin set with the clinician or equipment provider and seek help early. @D14,U17,U11,C07,T02
